head: The entry the ribbon does not cover
text: The file does not record — the file never records — that a younger man was posted to a station known to kill him, and did, and that the vacancy suited you. You know it. It is the one entry the ribbon does not cover.

head: A name in the small hours
text: Somewhere in the small hours you still hear the name of the boy you sent up-country to the fever, whose place fell conveniently vacant. No enquiry ever touched it. Nothing ever will, except you.

head: The blunder you buried
text: A young officer who would otherwise have been broken owes you his career and does not know it; you buried his blunder so deep that even he believes he never made it. It is the best thing you did all year, and it can never be told.

head: A rising man, bought early
text: Marked for the Division now — and Lala Hukum Chand keeps, in a red-bound ledger, the exact figure at which a rising man of Government was bought on easy terms, years before his price went up. He will never call it in. He does not need to. Owning you early is the whole art of the investment.

head: The Lala's sound investment
text: Lala Hukum Chand regards your year with the quiet satisfaction of a man reviewing a sound investment: whatever else you turned out to be, you were, in the end, his.

head: The morning you refused him
text: The Lala never forgave the morning you refused him to his face, and spent the year proving, in fees and grain-prices, that displeasure is only another line in the ledger. You were the poorer for it, and could look the bazaar in the eye, which is a currency he does not keep.

head: Ram Autar's one sentence
text: Old Ram Autar, who has outlasted six Collectors and will outlast you, allowed himself at the year’s end a single sentence of approval, in Persian, which you were not quite meant to catch and have not forgotten.

head: The clerk you lost
text: The head clerk asked for his pension in the cold weather and got it, correctly and coldly, and the record-room has never since given up its secrets to you at quite the old speed. You lost more than a clerk, and knew it too late.

head: Strickland's friendship
text: Strickland, who knows the district in ways the manuals do not admit exist, counts you a friend — which is worth more than a decoration and appears on no roll of honour.

head: Mrs Hauksbee's favour
text: Mrs Hauksbee, who has made and unmade more careers over the teacups of Simla than the Secretariat has, decided this year that she liked you; and things went, ever so slightly and quite untraceably, your way.

head: The understanding with the Pandit
text: Pandit Girdhari, who calls the whole edifice you serve a passing weather, nonetheless kept his side of a quiet understanding with you all year — two honest men on opposite sides of a thing neither of them made.

head: The case you were forbidden
text: The case Simla forbade you to touch stands settled and planted over, correct by every measure but the one that mattered to Simla, and it is the finest fortnight’s work of your year. It will appear in no report as long as you both shall live.

head: Gone soft on the native side
text: ‘Gone soft on the native side’ is the verdict of the billiard-room, delivered in the tone reserved for a good horse ruined; the district’s verdict, delivered in the tone reserved for the rarest of sahibs, is the opposite, and neither verdict will ever reach the other.

head: You learned the game
text: You learned the year’s real lesson early — that the district is governed for the report, and the report is written for Simla — and played it faultlessly, and the ribbon is the proof, and you are not certain, on the whole, that you are glad you learned it.

head: The broken-down Europeans
text: A handful of broken-down Europeans, the kind the Service prefers not to see, were quietly kept off the streets and out of the papers on your charity this year. It embarrassed everyone and saved two of them, which is a rate of return the Club would not understand.

head: A memsahib in the bungalow
text: You married this year, on an impulse the hot weather lent you and time has since ratified; there is a bungalow with curtains now, a child coming, and a reason to be home before dark. Whatever else the year cost you, you did not spend it alone, which the ribbon cannot say for every man who wears one.

head: The plains over the hills
text: You married, and then, when the hot weather came and she went up to the hills, you chose the plains and the district over the fortnight it would have taken to be a husband. A marriage learns its shape early out here, and yours learned that the district would always come first, which is true, and no comfort to the woman who married you not knowing it.

head: The lane you will not walk down
text: There was a house in the city once, this year, and a warmth in it the Club would have ended your career for; and you ended it yourself instead, cleanly, before it could. It was the prudent thing. You know the lane, and you do not walk down it, and you understand rather better now the sort of man the Service has been making of you.

head: The heart withdrawn
text: You kept the little house in the city and withdrew the heart from it — the arrangement maintained, the man withheld, the door of yourself shut against the one person who asked nothing of the Collector. She never reproached you. Her people have watched sahibs do as you did for a hundred years, and she asked for nothing, which is worse.

head: Married to the Service
text: You took no wife, kept no house, and gave the district the whole of a devotion another man would have spent on a family. Simla files you as the ideal officer, unencumbered and always available. The bungalow, at two in the morning, files you differently, and keeps its own counsel, as you have taught it to.

head: The decanter, each morning lower
text: It was never disgrace — nothing so definite — only a softening across the lonely months: a later start, a decanter each morning a finger lower than a careful man’s. The district noticed before you did; the district always does; and it keeps, in its long memory, a sorrowful column of the names of sahibs who drank alone.

head: Faith kept, unrecorded
text: You kept faith, this year, with people who could do nothing for you, at moments when no one was watching and it would have been easier not to. It is recorded nowhere. It is the only part of the year you would defend without flinching.

head: The girl from the Christmas camp
text: Five years of mail, one paper-chase, and a wire of eleven words: of everything the year decided, the October gangway at Bombay is the piece you would keep. The district got a memsahib who rides better than its Collector and misses nothing; the Collector got the only verdict of the season he never once rereads.

head: The year she was asked to add
text: Her letters still come, kind and complete and a page shorter than they were. You have banked one more year of her against the district’s ledger, at an interest neither of you names — and somewhere in Cheltenham a Thursday caller is patient too.

head: The generous letter
text: It was finely done, everyone would agree, if anyone were ever told: five years closed in three drafts, with every grace. The sandalwood box in Surrey is shut now. The bungalow’s long evenings have the shape of a door you built yourself, and painted, and locked.

head: Old paper, paid at sight
text: Sohan Lal’s book came up the country trade to meet you, and went home cancelled the same afternoon. In the bazaar’s oldest ledger — the one that prices signatures, not sums — the entry against your name now reads simply: good.

head: The footnote in the Lala's ledger
text: The Kotra book was never spoken of again, which is how such books do their work. It sits folded inside the district’s account like a seed in a fruit, and the Lala’s bow, year on year, keeps the particular warmth a banker reserves for his oldest security.

head: The ghost who signed at Kotra
text: You disowned the boy and his book in one even sentence, and the bazaar entered it the same evening. Nothing was ever said. Only, from that Friday, the district’s traders quoted the sirkar’s word at a rate fractionally under par — and never told you the discount’s name.

head: The dak that carries no stamps
text: The cutcherry worked for you from the first morning, and you did not have to ask why: a naib’s letter from Kotra had gone ahead, five years before the Gazette. The Service keeps two records of a man. The one that matters travels faster.

head: The munshi's dividend
text: Sujan Rai’s freezing cold-weather lessons paid out all season in a coin no treasury counts: cases that came to you straight, villages that spoke before they were spoken to, and a district that could not be got at through its interpreters. Somewhere in Kotra an old munshi remains, cautiously, proud.

head: The word 'exceptional', filed
text: The despatch that posted you here at four-and-twenty sits at the bottom of your confidential file like ballast, steadying everything written above it. Twice this year a doubt about you reached the Division and came back answered by a Collector’s red ink five years old.

head: The word 'economical'
text: The Kalapani has digested its bridge, and the enquiry’s finding follows you now from file to file: economical. Thirty-five thousand saved, a lakh drowned. Every officer in the province who reads your name this year reads that word beside it, and the ford drowns carts again as it always did.

head: The shoulder that reads the weather
text: The tigress of Salaiya left you a barometer set in bone and a name in the grass country that no Gazette can gazette. The gun-bearer who killed her on your body refused the reward and asked instead that his grandson be entered for the police. He was. The Service keeps some accounts properly.

head: The committal the bazaar remembers
text: The jury did what juries do, and the fine would not have kept Amherst in cartridges. It did not matter. What the district keeps is the committal itself, in your hand: the one season’s proof that the law could reach a sahib. The Club’s coldness will thaw in time. The other thing does not melt.

head: The exchange rate
text: Five thousand rupees, and the file closed as accident, and the Christmas shoot was the best in years. In the coolie lines they quote the figure still, without heat, as one quotes any settled market price. It is the only judgment you delivered this year that will be cited for a generation.

head: What the goddess did not forget
text: Three hundred graves at Tribeni, and no order of yours among the causes — only the absence where orders ought to have been. The enquiry was gentle. The burning-ghats were not. You trusted the river once, and the district will drink that year’s water for as long as you govern it.

head: Four cups of tea
text: No document records the conversations, and the compensation awards along the new line ran honest for the first time in railway memory. Strictly, the trust was breached; practically, it was spent where it was subscribed. You have decided which officer you are. The decision will not always be this cheap.
